result.stderr:
Usage:
  ef-timelapse <target-folder> [--out report.html] [--json report.json] [--mode auto|migrations|git]
  ef-timelapse serve <target-folder> [--mode auto|migrations|git] [--limit n] [--diff none|summary|full] [--port 5057] [--watch]

Options:
  --out <path>             Write a self-contained HTML report.
  --json <path>            Write the scan/replay model as JSON.
  --mode <mode>            auto, migrations, or git. Default: auto.
  --limit <n>              Limit Git mode to the latest n commits touching the target.
  --diff <mode>            Git diff payload: none, summary, or full. Default: summary.
  --max-diff-chars <n>     Max inline diff/preview chars per file. Default: 20000.
  --port <n>               Port for the local served viewer. Default: 5057.
  --watch                  In serve mode, rebuild the report after target-file changes.
  --no-cache               Disable the on-disk .ef-timelapse-cache index in Git mode; always re-walk full Git history.
  -h, --help               Show help.

The target can be a Migrations folder or a project/data folder containing one obvious Migrations child.
Auto mode uses migrations when present, otherwise Git scaffold history when the target is inside a Git repository.
`serve` uses the same auto-detection: one command works for either mode, and always opens the
interactive viewer (the Git-mode served UI, or the self-contained migration report) at the given port.
If no output option is supplied, JSON is written to stdout.
